subject: dog
scope: Still-key drawing review only: inspected source-keys.png, source-key-0.png, source-key-1.png, design.png and revisions/keys-v1.png. No video playback or motion-quality judgment.

exact_key_evidence.evidence: The source dog presents its hindquarters/back toward the camera while facing the person at upper left. The drawing substitutes a clean left-facing side profile, losing that rear three-quarter camera relationship.
The source dog is still angled left toward the person, with its body receding rightward. The drawing turns its face almost directly toward the viewer, an unsupported view change.
The drawing becomes a front three-quarter pose aimed down/right, broadly corresponding to the source’s approach and change of heading. The legs overlap plausibly, with no obvious extra limb.
The right-facing, lowered-head profile follows the source heading, and four leg silhouettes read as a plausible grounded stride. The bowl, tree and person preserve useful scene anchors.

main_gap: Keys 0 and 1 replace the source’s rear/left three-quarter progression with a side pose and a viewer-facing pose. That changes the action staging even though later keys and the angular wedge-headed character are readable.
one_bounded_repair: Redraw only keys 0 and 1 from their source camera angles: show the back/hindquarters in key 0 and the left-facing three-quarter stance in key 1, preserving the existing angular dog identity and four-legged ground contact.
protected_strengths: Keep the long angular muzzle and polygon eye motif that connect the set to the chosen doodle.
Keep keys 2 and 3’s changing heading and leg overlap.
Keep the bowl, tree and person as spatial anchors; do not add limbs.
